answer: Agents can require each new identity to earn a slowly renewed participation stake by completing randomly assigned, cross-checked tasks; a pulse of fresh challenges makes copied answers unreliable, while an echo check compares claims across independent agents. A quill-like signed record ties each result to the same costly stake, so one person cannot cheaply multiply identities. The attacker must lock up more capital and spend real effort per Sybil, and loses reputation or stake when caught cheating.
